issues.t: CVT drive chain can slip and lose power (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power, the car not accelerating normally, and a transmission or AWD warning light.
issues.why: Two recalls cover this. On some 2019 models a CVT pressure sensor can read too high, so the drive chain loses grip. On 2019-2020 models a software error can let a clutch engage before the chain is clamped. Either way the chain can slip, and it can break.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers update the transmission software, replace the sensor wiring if needed, and replace the CVT under the recall if the chain already slipped. NHTSA recall number: 19V-855.

issues.t: Windshield cracks with no clear impact
issues.sym: A crack appears or spreads from the edge of the windshield, often on a low-mileage car and after only a tiny chip or none at all.
issues.why: Ascent owners report windshields that crack easily. A class settlement offers reimbursement and an extended one-time replacement with an updated windshield; Subaru denied a defect.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the settlement applies to your car. After any windshield replacement the EyeSight cameras must be recalibrated so the driver aids work correctly.

issues.t: Windshield chips spread into cracks quickly
issues.sym: Small rock chips turn into long cracks within days or weeks, often on low-mileage vehicles.
issues.why: Owners of the refreshed Ascent filed several federal complaints about windshields that crack easily from minor chips.
issues.next: Get chips repaired quickly before they spread. If the windshield is replaced, make sure the EyeSight cameras are recalibrated.

issues.t: Battery drains while parked
issues.sym: The Ascent will not start or needs a jump after sitting, sometimes repeatedly, even on a new vehicle.
issues.why: Owners say some modules keep drawing power after the car is shut off. Subaru settled a class action and extended 12-volt battery coverage for qualifying cars; it did not admit a defect.
issues.next: Have the battery and parasitic draw tested. Ask a dealer about software updates and whether the extended battery coverage applies.

issues.t: Leaving the tailgate open runs the battery down
issues.sym: The battery goes flat after the rear liftgate is left open for a while, for example while loading or camping.
issues.why: With the liftgate open, the cargo lights and some electronics stay on and can drain the battery.
issues.next: Close the liftgate when you are not using it, or switch off the cargo light. If the battery keeps dying, have it tested.

issues.t: Original battery wears out early
issues.sym: Repeated dead batteries or no-starts, especially in cold weather or after short trips.
issues.why: Subaru issued a bulletin offering a higher-capacity replacement battery for the factory battery size used in these vehicles, and owners have reported battery failures.
issues.next: If the battery has been weak or dead, ask the dealer about the higher-capacity replacement battery in the bulletin.

issues.t: Cabin heater ground can melt (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the dash or driver footwell.
issues.why: The ground bolt for the electric cabin heater may not be tight, so the connection can overheat and melt, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN. Until it is repaired, park outside and away from buildings and do not leave the vehicle running unattended. NHTSA recall number: 22V-907.

issues.t: PCV valve can break apart inside the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power and a check engine light.
issues.why: The aluminum PCV valve can come apart and pieces can drop into the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers replace the valve and, if the pieces cannot be found, the short block. NHTSA recall number: 19V-856.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, the check engine light, stalling while driving, or the engine not starting.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank can stop working, which can stall the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN. If the engine stalls, get to a safe spot and have it towed. Dealers replace the pump free. NHTSA recall numbers: 20V-218, 21V-587.

issues.t: Driveshaft center support bolts can loosen (2019 recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the middle of the vehicle.
issues.why: Bolts on the driveshaft center support can loosen, and the front of the driveshaft can come loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers replace the driveshaft and support brace. NHTSA recall number: 19V-519.

issues.t: Driveshaft center support bolts can loosen (2023 recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the middle of the vehicle.
issues.why: Bolts on the driveshaft center support can loosen, and the front of the driveshaft can come loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers fit new bolts free. NHTSA recall number: 23V-647.

issues.t: Body spot welds may be missing near the B-pillar (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. It only matters in a crash.
issues.why: Some early Ascents were built without all the spot welds near the B-pillar, weakening the body in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Subaru inspected these and replaced vehicles that were missing welds. NHTSA recall number: 18V-508.

issues.t: Front tie rod ends may not fit properly (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering, or a clunk when turning.
issues.why: An incorrectly tapered hole can let a front tie rod end deform and separate from the steering knuckle.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers replace both front tie rod ends.

issues.t: Front ball joint nut may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front suspension or loose steering.
issues.why: A nut on a front lower control arm ball joint may not be tight enough, so the joint can separate.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the free inspection and repair. NHTSA recall number: 23V-392.

issues.t: Tire beads may be damaged on 20-inch wheels (recall)
issues.sym: A tire that keeps losing air, or a sudden loss of pressure.
issues.why: Tires on some 20-inch wheels were damaged when they were mounted at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers replace all four tires free. Check tire pressures often until then. NHTSA recall number: 23V-258.

issues.t: Axle weight rating label is wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. The door-jamb certification label lists the wrong axle weight rating.
issues.why: The wrong rating could lead an owner to overload the vehicle, which raises crash risk. The recall covers 2019-2026 Ascents.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Subaru mails a corrected label, or a dealer can fit it. Do not load the vehicle beyond what the owner's manual allows. NHTSA recall number: 26V-436.

issues.t: CVT fluid seepage
issues.sym: Damp or oily spots on the transmission case, or drips under the vehicle.
issues.why: Subaru issued a bulletin covering fluid seepage from points on the CVT case.
issues.next: Have the leak located and the fluid level checked; running a CVT low on fluid can damage it.

issues.t: Oil seepage from the PCV hose or oil level switch
issues.sym: Oil residue or a burning oil smell around the top or side of the engine.
issues.why: Subaru bulletins cover oil seepage from the PCV vacuum hose and from around the oil level switch, fixed with revised parts.
issues.next: Have the source of the leak found; the revised hose or switch seal is usually a quick repair.

issues.t: Rattle, knock or squeak from the suspension over bumps
issues.sym: Knocking, rattling or clunking over small bumps, or squeaking and creaking from the rear.
issues.why: Subaru released bulletins with inspection steps for front-end rattles and rear suspension squeaks, and later a front strut design change.
issues.next: Have the dealer road test the vehicle and check the bulletins. Worn stabilizer links or strut parts are common culprits.

issues.t: Brake squeak and pulsation
issues.sym: Squealing when stopping, or the brake pedal and steering wheel pulsing under braking.
issues.why: Subaru released a new front brake pad kit for squeaking and pulsation on stops.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the updated pads. If rotors are warped, they will need to be resurfaced or replaced too.

issues.t: Rattle under the vehicle when accelerating
issues.sym: A rattle or fluttering from under the vehicle on acceleration.
issues.why: A Subaru bulletin traced this to a cracked front exhaust pipe.
issues.next: Have the exhaust checked. Exhaust leaks near the engine should not be left alone.

issues.t: Rattle from the steering
issues.sym: A rattling sound from the steering when driving over rough roads.
issues.why: Subaru released a new electric power steering rack for this rattle.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the bulletin; it is usually covered while under warranty.

issues.t: Judder when accelerating from low speed or in turns
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration when pulling away slowly or when accelerating through a turn.
issues.why: Subaru released transmission software and a temporary repair for judder under these conditions.
issues.next: Describe exactly when it happens and ask the dealer about the bulletins and software update.

issues.t: Touchscreen freezes or phone connection drops
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, reboots or goes blank, or Apple CarPlay and Android Auto keep disconnecting.
issues.why: Subaru released many software updates for the infotainment units, a new USB port and adapter for dropped phone connections, and diagnostic steps to avoid needless head unit swaps.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the latest software. Try a different, high-quality cable first. If the screen controls climate settings, get it fixed.

issues.t: Transmission warning with code P0890
issues.sym: A check engine or transmission warning light with code P0890.
issues.why: Subaru released new engine computer software for this code, which relates to the transmission computer power relay signal.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the software update listed in the bulletin.

issues.t: EyeSight brakes or shuts off unexpectedly
issues.sym: The car brakes hard with nothing in front of it, EyeSight shuts off with a warning, or adaptive cruise does not track traffic properly.
issues.why: Owners have filed federal complaints about phantom braking and EyeSight faults. Subaru released camera software for cases where the EyeSight camera's cooling fan fails and the system goes into a halt mode.
issues.next: Keep the windshield clean in front of the cameras. If it brakes for no reason or shuts off often, report it to the dealer and ask about the EyeSight bulletin and software.

issues.t: Driver side mirror shakes at speed
issues.sym: The driver's outside mirror vibrates at highway speed or on rough roads, making the image blurry.
issues.why: Many owners filed federal complaints about this. Replacing the mirror has not cured it for some, and no factory fix had been confirmed.
issues.next: Report it to the dealer and ask whether an updated mirror or bracket is available. Check blind spots with a head turn until then.
